editorial_principle: Selection is by structural explanatory value and breadth, not alphabetical order or frequency in earlier AI conversation.

featured_cases.label: Canada
featured_cases.why: Shows Payments Canada, Interac and the Bank of Canada as different institutions, and separate scheme/clearing/settlement roles.
featured_cases.comparison: UK has different scheme governance and access model; neither represents the whole world.

featured_cases.label: Wise
featured_cases.why: Shows an institution spanning customer interface, multi-market accounts, FX and last-mile payout functions; roles vary by market.
featured_cases.comparison: Another multi-market provider; featured company does not imply market leadership or all corridors.

featured_cases.label: Pix (Brazil)
featured_cases.why: Demonstrates a distinct model: BCB owns Pix scheme, operates SPI settlement and DICT directory, and permits different participation arrangements.
featured_cases.comparison: NPCI/UPI illustrates a different operator/central-bank relationship; Pix chosen to contrast Canada.

specialized_case.why: Shows a USD-to-USD cross-border payment that still crosses legal and banking jurisdictions; not selected for market scale.

market_selection_criteria: payment-system scale and relevance from operator/regulator statistics
variation by geography, language and payment type
corridor relevance and end-user delivery mechanisms
independent official evidence and its date
